comments.author: @AmongTheNoneOfUs
comments.text:
One of my favorite comic strips goes like this:

guy 1: Some day we won't even need coders any more. We'll be able to just write the specification and the program will write itself.
guy 2: Oh wow, you're right! We'll be able to write a comprehensive and precise spec and bam, we won't need programmers any more!
guy 1: Exactly!
guy 2: And do you know the industry term for a project specification that is comprehensive and precise enough to generate a program?
guy 1: uh... no...
guy 2: Code. It's called code.

In my opinion, if you need a program to do something specific, maybe you can make the ai do it with natural language, but by the time you get done specifying exactly how the program should function, you'll have been better off learning to code and specifying the program in code, especially due to maintenance reasons. I think code will be infinitely easier to edit and debug than a program specified in natural language and given to an ai which then makes the "real" program.

Maybe the ai could get you a program that is close to doing everything you want it to do, and then you could debug the program to fix the behaviors that aren't quite right... you'll have to get good at debugging in the output language, and good luck understanding a complex program if you didn't write it yourself...

Okay, so maybe the ai just produces simple programs, or maybe the way you improve on a program is feeding back to the ai that the program doesn't quite behave the way you'd like, and so you specify what should be changed... I think it's just a round about way of coding in the end. In the end, you'll have specified every little detail of this complex program that you need, you won't understand any of the output code that you would have understood if you had learned to code and programmed it yourself, and now you've got this long list of natural language commands to the ai that may not be as easy to move around in the specification of the program, in order to simplify the specification, as it would be to move around if it was written in code.

Your idea of having some prompts which you have saved and that you give to the ai agent to complete, you could probably also write a program in code to do that... I think the ai agent is going the long way around to avoid something that is actually easier; learning to code so that you can write programs to automate tasks, especially tasks which are repetitive.

Maybe it'll just be another tool for developers to get stuff done. In essence, it's just another dependency or build system. For instance, "download this ai agent, and give it this commands file, then run the program" etc... I'm sure it won't be a very small dependency though.

I don't know. It could be cool. I just don't see the use case yet and haven't been impressed by anything I've seen. So far all I've seen is automation of tasks in the "low hanging fruit" category, such as cloning a repository, following install instructions, etc... and that in itself is commendable... but I have not seen automation of tasks in the "make tools which make human life easier and more enjoyable" category... For that, I suspect we will always need people who know how to code.
